hints.title: Jump Destination Criteria
hints.text: From index i, you can jump to the next greater-or-equal element, or to the next strictly smaller element.

hints.title: Precomputing Valid Transitions
hints.text: Use two monotonic stacks to compute next_ge[i] and next_smaller[i] for all indices.

hints.title: Dynamic Cost Propagation
hints.text: Maintain dp[i] as the minimum cost to reach index i. Forward propagate dp[i] to its valid jump destinations.

hints.title: Monotonic Jump Transitions Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minCost(self, nums: list[int], costs: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        dp = [float("inf")] * n
        dp[0] = 0
        
        stk_ge = []
        stk_lt = []
        
        for i in range(n):
            while stk_ge and nums[i] >= nums[stk_ge[-1]]:
                prev = stk_ge.pop()
                dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[prev] + costs[i])
            stk_ge.append(i)
            
            while stk_lt and nums[i] < nums[stk_lt[-1]]:
                prev = stk_lt.pop()
                dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[prev] + costs[i])
            stk_lt.append(i)
            
        return dp[n - 1]
```

complexity.notes: Each index is pushed and popped at most once in each monotonic stack.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all O(n^2) pairs to find valid jumps takes quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two monotonic stacks and dp array of size n.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate identifies that the problem rules define jumps precisely to next greater-or-equal and next smaller elements.
